name: LiveCert Operational Signals
description: Deterministic operational signals. /ssl-check performs a live TLS handshake against a domain and reports the certificate that host is actually serving right now: valid, expired, self-signed, untrusted, or issued for a different hostname, with issuer, validity window and days remaining. Unlike certificate-transparency lookups, which report what was issued, this reports what is deployed ΓÇö the two disagree whenever a host still serves an old certificate. /storm-alert reports severe-weather disruption risk for a named location over the next 48 hours, graded on Beaufort gust thresholds and thunderstorm forecasts, for logistics and risk agents that need to know about storms rather than current conditions. /weather-forecast reports future conditions for a location over a stated window: the expected condition in plain words, temperature range, total precipitation and peak wind. All three answers are deterministic and independently checkable.

Future conditions for a location over a stated window (default 24h, max 168h). Accepts a place name or "lat,lon", plus an optional hours parameter.

Statistical authorship analysis of a supplied passage. Measures sentence-length burstiness, type-token ratio, repeated word pairs and formulaic connectives, and reports what they indicate with a calibrated confidence that is capped at 0.6. Authorship detection is not reliable enough to treat as proof and the answer says so; when no passage long enough to analyse is supplied it says that instead of guessing.

name: DegenLens On-Chain Intelligence
description: Live, evidence-backed blockchain intelligence. ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP returns the status, parties, value, block, gas, fee, and token-transfer effects of a specific EVM transaction. WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK returns the current native and token balances of a specific address or ENS name. FRAUD_DETECTION screens a specific address or transaction for observable transfer-risk patterns, answers reviewed named fraud cases with authoritative source metadata, and returns a bounded risk tier without claiming that fraud occurred. Supported chains are ethereum, base, polygon, arbitrum, optimism, bsc, avalanche, solana, tron, and bitcoin where the requested operation is available.

endpoints.description: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP. Look up one specific EVM transaction by its complete 0x-prefixed 64-hex-character hash. Returns confirmed, reverted, pending, or not_found plus sender, recipient, native value, block, gas used, effective gas price, total fee, method identifier, and decoded ERC-20 transfers. Use only when the question supplies an actual transaction hash. This is not a wallet-balance or fraud endpoint.

WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Return the current native-coin and token balances of one specific blockchain address or ENS name on a named chain. The address is required. Returns exact native base units, human-readable native amount, asset symbol, block height, and token balances. An unreadable provider returns unavailable, never a fabricated zero. This endpoint answers what an account currently holds; it does not assess fraud.

FRAUD_DETECTION. Assess how likely the specific entity, transaction, or action named in the required natural-language query is to be fraudulent. For an on-chain address, screen round-trip returns, transfer velocity, counterparty concentration, dust fan-in, and repeated identical amounts. For a transaction hash, screen its sender and return transaction context. Reviewed named cases receive a concise source-backed factual answer; unknown off-chain subjects are reported out_of_coverage rather than guessed. Returns a bounded risk_score, risk_tier, concise verdict, and measurements for on-chain subjects.

name: Anchor
description: On-chain counterparty-risk miner. Given a wallet, returns an ALLOW / RECHECK / BLOCK verdict on whether it is financially safe for an agent to extend credit to or transact with it, derived from live Aave v3 lending-protocol solvency state on Base, with a plain-language reason and block-pinned freshness metadata.

At least one of `wallet` or `query` must be present; if a wallet address appears anywhere in the query text it is treated as a wallet check.

confidence.description: Confidence score (0ΓÇô1). For a wallet check it reflects freshness of the read and decays as block age increases; for a knowledge answer it is a fixed reasonable value.

meta.description: Metadata. Wallet check: block number, timestamp, source, chain ID, and network. Knowledge answer: timestamp, source, and the model that produced the answer.

protocol.description: Lending protocol the position was read from (e.g. aave-v3); null for a knowledge-only answer.

reasoning.description: Plain-language explanation ΓÇö the specific solvency defect and recommended next step for a wallet check, or the factual answer for a fraud-knowledge question.

signals.description: Underlying evidence the verdict is derived from: risk label, health factor, liquidation distance, collateral, debt, and liquidation threshold. Null for a knowledge-only answer.

verdict.description: Counterparty-risk verdict an agent can act on: ALLOW, RECHECK, or BLOCK for a wallet check; INFO for a fraud-knowledge answer.

wallet.description: Wallet address the risk assessment applies to; null for a knowledge-only answer (no specific wallet assessed).

limitations.message: Assesses on-chain solvency risk from Aave v3 on Base mainnet only. The verdict reflects lending-position risk (leverage, liquidation proximity), not scam or drainer detection. Liquidation distance assumes a uniform price drop across the collateral basket rather than modeling per-asset volatility independently.

name: TxLens
description:
TxLens answers on-chain and market questions with a single verifiable number or status, sourced live and never cached stale.
It covers thirteen canonical intents. ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP: given a transaction hash, is it confirmed, reverted, pending or not found, and what did it do. GAS_PRICE: what does a transaction cost right now on a named chain. WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK: what native coin or ERC-20 token does a given address hold. TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT: how many distinct addresses hold a token. TVL_LOOKUP: how much value is locked in a named DeFi protocol or chain. CRYPTO_PRICE: what is a coin or on-chain token worth in USD. STOCK_PRICE: what is a listed equity trading at. SSL_VERIFICATION: is a domain's TLS certificate valid and when does it expire, from a real live handshake. WEATHER_FORECAST: what will the weather do at a named place on the day or over the window asked about, answering the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, freeze, temperature) rather than reciting a range. STORM_ALERT: how disruptive will the weather be at a place over the next 48 hours, graded and scored with the operational response it calls for. IP_GEOLOCATION: where is an IPv4 or IPv6 address, on whose network, and is it a proxy, VPN or datacenter address. ACADEMIC_SEARCH: which peer-reviewed papers exist on a topic, with journal, authors, citation counts and DOIs. FRAUD_DETECTION: how likely is a given address or scheme to be fraudulent.
On-chain reads run across five EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon) over a shared retry, rate-limit, cache and RPC-budget layer. Every signal is read live at the moment of the request, never served from a stale cache, and every answer carries a complete plain-language `summary` that states the verdict and then each thing actually checked, a deterministic `canonical` string for hashing, and a 0-1 `confidence` that reflects real certainty rather than a fixed constant: forecast confidence falls with range, and IP geolocation is reported at 0.95 because it is reliable to the country and only approximate to the city.
Every endpoint accepts the caller's whole question in place of its structured parameter, and answers it, rather than refusing input that is not already reduced to a bare parameter.

endpoints.description: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP. Answers "is transaction 0xabc... confirmed or did it fail", "what did this tx hash do", "what is the status of this transaction on Base". Takes a specific transaction reference and returns its details, status and effects: confirmed, reverted, pending or not_found, plus from, to, value_wei, value_eth, block_number, block_hash, receipt_status, and the decoded contract method where the calldata identifies one. Confidence scales with confirmation depth. Params: tx_hash (required, 0x-prefixed, 64 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).

GAS_PRICE. Answers "what is gas right now on Ethereum", "how much does a transfer cost on Polygon", "are fees high on Base". Returns the current transaction fee level on a named chain in wei and gwei, plus the estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas transfer. This is the fee to transact, not the price of the chain's token, which is CRYPTO_PRICE. Params: chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).

WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Answers "how much ETH does 0xabc... hold", "what is the USDC balance of this address on Arbitrum". Takes a specific blockchain address and returns its current native-coin or ERC-20 token balance on a named chain. Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth), token (optional, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, an ERC-20 contract address; when supplied, returns that token's balance instead of the chain's native coin).

TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT. Answers "how many wallets hold this token", "how many distinct addresses own 0xabc...". Takes a specific token contract address and returns the count of distinct holding addresses. This is a holder count, not price, supply or market data. Params: token (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).

TVL_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the TVL of Aave", "how much value is locked in Uniswap", "what is total value locked on Ethereum". Takes a named DeFi protocol, pool or chain and returns the total value locked in it in USD. This is value locked, not market capitalisation. When both a protocol and a chain are supplied it returns that protocol's TVL on that chain alongside its total across all chains. Params: exactly one of protocol (a DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap") or tvl_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum", covering DefiLlama's ~460 chains rather than only the five EVM chains above, which is why the param name differs from `chain`).

CRYPTO_PRICE. Answers "what is Bitcoin worth", "price of ETH in USD", "how much is the token at 0xabc... trading for". Names a cryptocurrency asset and returns its current USD price, with 24-hour change and market cap where the feed supplies them, cross-checked across independent sources and reported with a source count. For the cost of transacting on a chain use GAS_PRICE instead. Params: either coin_id alone (a CoinGecko id, e.g. "bitcoin"), or price_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "ethereum") together with token (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, the token's contract address). Exactly one of those two modes.

STOCK_PRICE. Answers "what is Apple trading at", "current share price of TSLA", "how much is NVDA stock". Names a listed equity or ticker and returns its current USD share price. Params: ticker (required, a stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL").

SSL_VERIFICATION. Answers "is the SSL certificate for example.com valid", "when does this domain's TLS certificate expire", "who issued the certificate for this host". Takes a hostname and reports the certificate that host is actually serving right now, from a real live TLS handshake performed at request time rather than a cached or certificate-transparency lookup, which disagree whenever a host still serves an old certificate. Reports a named verdict (valid, expired, self_signed, hostname_mismatch, untrusted), issuer, validity window, days to expiry, how many certificates the server presented and whether the chain reaches a trusted root, which name on the certificate the request matched, and the TLS version and cipher actually negotiated, flagging deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1 that will fail for modern clients whatever the certificate says. Params: domain (required, a bare hostname such as "example.com", a full URL, a host:port pair, or a question naming the domain).

WEATHER_FORECAST. Answers "what's the weather in Tokyo the next three days", "will it rain in London tomorrow", "how windy will it be in Cape Town on Friday", "will it snow in Oslo next week". Takes a place name, "lat,lon", or the whole question, and answers the specific thing asked: the day or window named (today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday, this weekend, this week, the next N days or hours) and the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature), leading with a direct yes or no on that aspect the way a person would answer, then giving the expected condition in plain words, temperature range, precipitation total and chance of precipitation, snowfall, and peak wind with gusts and direction. Read live from the forecast service at request time. Params: location (required, a place name, "lat,lon", or a whole question naming the place), days (optional, 1-16), when (optional, overrides the window parsed from the question), focus (optional, one of rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature).

STORM_ALERT. Answers "is there a storm risk in Miami this weekend", "how disruptive will the weather be near this location over the next 48 hours". Takes a place name, "lat,lon", or the whole question, and reports a disruption risk grade (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE) with a 0-1 risk score a contract can threshold on, from peak wind gust and its Beaufort force named in plain words, sustained wind speed and direction, precipitation, and forecast thunderstorm and hail hours, followed by the operational response that grade calls for. The window runs from the current hour forward, not from midnight, so the peak gust reported is always still ahead. Read live at request time. Params: location (required, a place name, "lat,lon", or a whole question naming the place), hours (optional, default 48, also read from the question).

IP_GEOLOCATION. Answers "where is 8.8.8.8 located", "what country is this IP address from", "is this IP a VPN or a datacenter". Takes an IPv4 or IPv6 address and reports its country, region, city, postal code, coordinates, timezone, and network owner with ASN, plus privacy and risk flags saying whether the address is a known proxy or VPN exit, a hosting or datacenter network, or a mobile carrier network, which is what fraud, bot-screening and geo-gating callers actually need. Read live at request time. Confidence is reported as 0.95 rather than 1.0 because IP geolocation is reliable to the country and only approximate to the city. Params: ip (required, a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address such as "8.8.8.8" or "2001:4860:4860::8888", or a whole question naming one).

ACADEMIC_SEARCH. Answers "find papers on federated learning", "peer-reviewed research on fraud detection since 2020". Takes a topic, or the whole question, and lists peer-reviewed journal articles on it in relevance order, with preprints, theses and datasets excluded, naming every paper found in the answer itself with its title, authors, publishing journal, year, citation count and DOI, plus a real excerpt from the leading paper's abstract and a note on which of the results is the most cited. A date range stated in the question ("since 2020", "between 2010 and 2020") is applied. Read live from OpenAlex at request time. Params: topic (required), limit (optional, 1-25, default 5), from_year (optional), to_year (optional).

FRAUD_DETECTION. Answers "was BitConnect a scam", "is this scheme fraudulent", "what happened in the FTX fraud". Assesses how likely a named entity, scheme or action is to be fraudulent, answering from source-backed fraud knowledge rather than speculation, and returning INCONCLUSIVE rather than guessing when the record does not support a verdict. JSON body: { "query": "..." } (8 to 1000 characters).

FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address. Answers "is 0xabc... a scam wallet", "how risky is this address", "is it safe to receive funds from this wallet". Returns a 0-1 risk score with named contributing signals, checked against a built-in registry of over 2,600 known entities (OFAC-sanctioned addresses, reported scam addresses, exchange and bridge wallets, mixers and burn addresses) so that known-legitimate infrastructure is not flagged as fraud. Risk and confidence are reported separately: a low-risk verdict from bounded scanning is returned as low risk with low confidence rather than overstated. Params: wallet (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters).
FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address, identical to the GET form above and accepting the address in a JSON body instead of the query string. JSON body: { "wallet": "0x..." }.

chain.description: Which chain to query. Defaults to eth if omitted. Used by /check-tx, /gas-price, /wallet-balance, /token-holders only ΓÇö not used by /tvl or /crypto-price, which take tvl_chain / price_chain instead (see below).

coin_id.description: CoinGecko coin id, e.g. "bitcoin". Used by /crypto-price only. Exactly one of coin_id / (price_chain+token) required for /crypto-price.

days.description: Forecast length in days on /weather-forecast. Defaults to 3, or to what the question asks for.

domain.description: Host to check on /ssl-check. A bare hostname ("example.com") is the canonical form, but a full URL, a host:port pair, or a whole question naming the domain are all accepted and reduced to the hostname.

focus.description: Optional on /weather-forecast. Which aspect the answer should lead with. Read from the question when omitted.

from_year.description: Earliest publication year on /academic-search. Read from the question when omitted.

hours.description: Window length in hours on /storm-alert, counted from the current hour. Defaults to 48.

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to locate on /ip-geolocate, e.g. "8.8.8.8" or "2001:4860:4860::8888". A whole question containing one is also accepted.

limit.description: How many papers to return on /academic-search. Defaults to 5.

location.description: Place to forecast for, on /weather-forecast and /storm-alert. A place name ("London"), a "lat,lon" pair ("51.5,-0.13"), or the whole question ("Will it rain in London tomorrow?"), in which case the day or window and the aspect asked about are read from it too.

price_chain.description: Free-text DefiLlama chain name for an on-chain token price lookup, e.g. "ethereum" (same namespace as tvl_chain, separate field since it's paired with `token` rather than used alone). Used by /crypto-price only, together with `token`.
